slides.title: Slide - What is Prompting?
slides.narration:
Let's begin by understanding what prompting means.
In simple words, prompting means telling an Al exactly what you want it to do.
Good prompting skills help you to get the best from Al.
Prompting is a skill of writing clear and specific instructions to Al to get the right output.
slides.image_prompt:
Slide - "Understand: Why Clarity Matters" Now, let's understand why clear prompts matter.
Visual: Person typing vague prompt vs. clear prompt, side by side

slides.narration:
Think of Al as a child who is curious, intelligent, fast, and eager to help.
Al is capable, but it relies on your instructions to perform well.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration: A bright, curious child raising their hand eagerly

slides.narration:
Like a child, Al follows instructions literally.
It cannot read your mind or guess your intent.
It follows exactly what you tell it to do.

Imagine telling a child, “Clean the room.”
That's vague.
The child may pick up a few things and think the job is done.
So vague instructions give vague results.
slides.image_prompt: Scene: Adult telling child vaguely "Clean the room" child only picks up a few toys

slides.narration:
Now, let's think about how to explain the "clean the room" task to a child.
Break it into simple parts and give clear instructions.
So you can say, "Put all the toys in the box.
Fold the clothes and keep them in the cupboard.
Arrange the books on the shelf."
Now the child knows exactly what to do and does the job well.
Structured guidance and clear steps give better outcomes.
slides.image_prompt: Scene: Adult giving step-by-step instructions child follows happily

slides.narration:
Al works the same way.
A vague prompt gives a vague answer.
A clear prompt gives a desired answer.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: vague vs clear instruction to child

slides.narration: Prompting is the art and science of guiding Al to produce desired results.
slides.image_prompt: Text highlight: “Prompting = giving instructions to Al"

slides.narration:
A good Al prompt should do 4 things.
It should say exactly what you want.
For example, put all the toys in the box.
Next, it should give a relevant background.
For example, fold the clothes and keep them in the cupboard.
It should also mention how the output should appear.
For example, arrange the books on the shelf.
Finally, it should specify why you need it.
For example, the room should look clean and tidy.
A good prompt can do tasks like writing, designing, brainstorming, and coding.
slides.image_prompt: Montage of outputs: text, code, images, tables

slides.narration: It can even help analyze data or create images without coding skills.

slides.title: Summary Slide
slides.narration:

In this tutorial, we learned,

• Clear prompts lead to better Al results.
• Structured steps make prompts powerful.
